evidence.quote: In the MDF process, the specimens are forged sequentially in the x, y and z directions (X-Y-Z-X … , as shown in Fig. 1 ), and the forging speed is 1 mm/s.
The forged material was also subjected to T5 treatment at 180 ◦ C, 190 ◦ C, 200 ◦ C, 210 ◦ C and 220 ◦ C to obtain the microstructure and mechanical properties of the final state.

The cast alloy is mainly composed of α -Mg, with a large number of dendritic second phases (marked by red circles) and a few rounded second phases (marked by red boxes) distributed around the grain boundaries
The atomic composition of the dendritic second phase obtained from the energy spectrum analysis is Mg-8.11%Gd-2.34%Y-6.32%Zn, which can be tentatively confirmed as Mg 3 (Gd,Y) phase
The atomic composition of the square phase at C is Mg-13.11%Gd-24.99%Y, which has been proved to be a RE-rich phase with FCC structure by existing studies
the round block phase at D is a phase formed by the polarization of Zr elements with a composition of up to 75.74%.

These substructures undergo subgrain boundary rotation with MDF deformation, which increases the orientation difference with the original grains and forms a series of fine DRXed grains.

it is difficult to coordinate deformation by grain boundary sliding in a small number of coarse grains within the microstructure, which is the reason for a large number of twins occurring within the grains.
Because grain refinement to the micron level, the contribution of grain boundary sliding increases and may even dominate the deformation
The strengthening effect of these precipitated phases works together with the grain boundary strengthening effect from grain refinement to ensure the increase in alloy strength.
Due to the strengthening of the fine precipitates under peak aging, the YS increased from 324.7 MPa to 395.2 MPa
The increase in alloy strength is related to solid solution strengthening and is more attributed to the combined effect of grain refinement and aging precipitation.
